prayerExcerpt.en-US: The least suffering for the faith, borne with humility and courage, is the proof that Christ has heard our prayer.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: O menor sofrimento pela fé, suportado com humildade e coragem, é a prova de que Cristo ouviu a nossa oração.

meta.face: An Alexandrian woman of about sixty-five with a warm olive complexion and a SHORT, WIDE face — a BROAD, LOW forehead, smooth, full cheeks and a SMALL, soft, rounded chin; very LARGE, dark, luminous eyes, CLOSE-SET, like those of a Fayum portrait, under THICK, strongly ARCHED black brows flecked with grey that nearly MEET above the nose; a LONG, slender nose with a narrow bridge and a gentle HOOK; a small, full mouth closed calmly; fine lines at the eyes; a few grey-streaked black waves showing under the veil; her gaze lifted a little, steadfast.
meta.basis: No likeness survives. The book, following Dionysius of Alexandria, calls her 'an aged virgin' (the Catholic Encyclopedia reads virgo presbytera as possibly a deaconess), so she is shown old, not as the young girl of Zurbarán; the pincers holding a tooth are her sign in art (Catholic Encyclopedia). The Fayum-portrait eyes and brows, a real Roman Egyptian type, are our choice for the structure.
